neighbours.label: the Great Lakes and Rust Belt region on both sides of the border (Lake Erie and Lake Michigan shores, Ohio, Buffalo, Syracuse, Detroit, Pittsburgh, Toledo and the Ontario lakeshore), named or not; places in the South, the Southwest and on the Pacific coast stay low (lake country elsewhere in the north can read weakly, and is not tested here)
fire: Commuters in Syracuse shoveled out after another lake-effect storm.
The steel town of Youngstown is trying to reinvent itself.
Ford's assembly line in Dearborn added a night shift.
Charter boats chase walleye off Port Clinton every summer.
Hamilton's harbour once smelled of the steel mills.
The Bills played through a blizzard in Orchard Park.
Cargo ships unload at the docks of Toledo.
Pittsburgh's old mill sites along the Monongahela are now parks.
quiet: Commuters in Phoenix waited out another dust storm.
The mining town of Bisbee is trying to reinvent itself.
Boeing's assembly line in Everett added a night shift.
Charter boats chase redfish off Port Aransas every summer.
Savannah's harbour once smelled of the paper mills.
The Dolphins played through a downpour in Miami Gardens.
Cargo ships unload at the docks of Long Beach.
San Antonio's old mission sites along the river are now parks.
